metaTitle: WhatheRust: a lightweight WhatsApp desktop app built with Rust
metaDescription: An unofficial, open-source WhatsApp desktop client for Windows, macOS and Linux. Built with Rust and Tauri, it uses your system's webview instead of bundling a browser.
heroTitle: WhatsApp on your desktop, without a bundled browser
heroSubtitle: WhatheRust is a lightweight, unofficial WhatsApp desktop client written in Rust with Tauri. It runs WhatsApp Web in your operating system's own webview instead of shipping a copy of Chromium.
disclaimer: Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by WhatsApp Inc. or Meta Platforms, Inc. WhatsApp is a trademark of its owner.
noReleases: The first release is on its way.
unsigned: Builds are not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper may warn on first launch.
featuresIntro: Everything here is in the app today.
featureWebviewBody: Uses WebView2 on Windows, WKWebView on macOS and WebKitGTK on Linux. No bundled browser engine.
featureSizeBody: The Linux .deb is {size}, because the browser engine is already part of your system.
featureTrayBody: Closing the window hides it to the tray. Click the tray icon to bring it back, or quit from its menu.
featureNotificationsBody: New messages show up as regular system notifications.
featureLoginBody: Your WhatsApp session is kept in the app's own data folder, so you scan the QR code once.
featureSingleBody: Launching it again focuses the window that is already open instead of starting a second copy.
featureLinksBody: Only WhatsApp pages load inside the app. Everything else opens in your default browser.
featureLookTitle: Looks at home on each OS
featureLookBody: Mica and rounded corners on Windows 11, and a title bar tinted to match WhatsApp on macOS.
featureUpdatesBody: The app checks GitHub Releases on launch and asks before installing a signed update.

shotQrCaption: Log in by scanning the QR code with your phone.

compareIntro: Electron apps ship their own copy of Chromium and Node.js. To see what that costs, we built the same WhatsApp Web wrapper with Electron and measured both on the same Linux machine.
compareOfficial: What about the official app? There is no official WhatsApp app for Linux, and on Windows it now loads web.whatsapp.com in a WebView2 container rather than Electron. We could not measure it on the same machine, so it is not in the chart.
changelogIntro: Every release of WhatheRust, straight from GitHub Releases.
changelogEmpty: No releases yet. The first one will show up here as soon as it is published.
footerBuilt: Built with Rust, Tauri and SvelteKit.
compareMemoryNote: Memory goes the other way on Linux: in our test, WebKitGTK used more memory than Electron's Chromium at the login screen. We show it anyway. Windows and macOS use different webviews, which we could not measure here.
compareMethod: Measured on {date} on Ubuntu 22.04.5 (x86_64, WebKitGTK 2.50.4) in a virtual machine. WhatheRust 0.1.0 release build against a minimal Electron 45.0.0 wrapper (electron-builder 26.18.0) that loads the same page with the same user agent. Sizes are the built .deb and AppImage files. Memory: fresh profile on the WhatsApp Web QR login screen, 60 s idle, then the median of 5 samples taken 10 s apart, summing resident memory (RSS) over the whole process tree, including WebKit's web and network processes and Electron's helper processes.
